Implementation approach: Bob here. We'll preserve C++ protocol files exactly: CMakeLists.txt, src/Main.cpp as the runtime entry, and tests/test_main.cpp as the single test file. The core domain is split into small, concrete, reusable modules with 1:1 include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs: Geometry (grid and direction utilities), Entities (Arena, Tank, Projectile), and Game (orchestration of ticks, commands, collisions, scoring). The runtime demo remains thin and non-interactive. All domain logic is pure and deterministic: no IO, no OS-specific behavior, no randomness, and no timing. Tests include headers only, link against the core library, and remain headless/offline. The architecture targets 9 files to meet the 8–10 file goal while keeping responsibilities clear and minimal.

Anything UNCLEAR: Assumptions made for determinism: origin at (0,0) top-left with x increasing right and y increasing down; default tank health=3; damage per hit=1; one projectile spawned per Fire command if muzzle cell is in-bounds and free of obstacles/tanks; no fire rate limiting beyond cell occupancy; winner is set to the opponent when one tank reaches 0 health; if both die in the same tick, winner remains unset.
